messages:
mira: Quick sync—thinking about a tighter interface to let runtime mix FP8 + 4-bit within a single top-level request. current profiles force a single precision lane per model invocation which is painful for multi-task prompts.

josh: +1. can you sketch the main goals? is this about per-layer selection, per-token, or profile-level blending?

mira: Mainly two things: 1) allow per-layer profile hints from scheduler (cheap) 2) allow opt-in per-request overrides (customer/endpoint-level) so we can do targeted high-fidelity on sensitive spans. not full token-wise yet.

anita: Sounds good. concern: where do we draw boundary between "profile hints" and "hard contracts"? ops needs a deterministic fallback path.

kai: Runtime perspective: implement as a lightweight vector of (layer-range -> precision) attached to request metadata. scheduler can synthesize it. If missing, fallback to profile table.

mira: Exactly. example payload idea: 
```json
{"precision_hints": [{"start_layer": 0, "end_layer": 3, "precision": "fp8"}, {"start_layer": 4, "end_layer": -1, "precision": "4bit"}], "hint_type": "soft"}
```
Where hint_type = soft|enforced.

josh: Nice. For "soft" hints runtime can try to run in cheaper lane but must record deviation metrics and optionally escalate to enforced if degradation detected.

anita: Ops asks for these guardrails: a max-deg (loss-of-quality threshold), telemetry hooks that link to prompt ids, and automatic revert to enforced=fp8 if SLO/deg triggers.

kai: Telemetry is doable. We'll emit per-request: applied_profile, attempted_profile, fallback_reason, rand_seed_for_sampling, and degscore_estimate. need schema.

mira: Agree. devex: we should keep SDK UX simple. devex-bot: Recommend adding a helper: client.precisionHints([...]) + validators. Also doc snippets and a canary flag.

devex-bot: Draft suggestion: keep top-level API param `precision_overrides` optional; if present server validates size and rejects > 16 entries to avoid O(N) overhead.

josh: Performance note: switching precision mid-run may require reloading kernels or switching execution paths. keep hints aligned to contiguous layer ranges to minimize kernel switches. enforce that in validation.

anita: Operational rollout: 1) internal-only experiments with shadow traffic, 2) small canary customers with opt-in, 3) add automatic rollback if degradation > X% for 1h.

kai: Implementation plan (short): - parser in front-door to translate hints into runtime plan - scheduler passes plan to serving workers - workers validate contiguous ranges & merge adjacent same-precision ranges - apply kernels with minimal switches - emit telemetry to precision-telemetry stream.

mira: Can someone pick up the RFC follow-up doc? we should include sample telemetry schema, validation rules, and a short test plan.

josh: I'll draft the RFC follow-up. will include unit tests for merge logic + perf bench script.

anita: I'll own the canary and rollback playbook. adding ops checklist to runbook.

kai: I'll prototype the worker merge/emit logic. expect a draft in ~3 days.

ops-bot: Deploy scheduled: queuing canary infra resources after approval. :gear:

mira: Thanks all. next check-in Friday after drafts. :thumbsup:
